items.title: Delhi High Court strikes down 65-year retirement age for photographers at Taj Mahal, other ASI monuments
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has struck down the Archaeological Survey of India's (ASI) decision to impose a retirement age of 65 years on licensed photographers working at the Taj Mahal and other centrally protected monuments. A bench of Justices Prathiba M Singh and Dinesh Bhatt held that the restriction was discriminatory and adversely affected their right to livelihood. It said that the photographers, who are self-employed professionals and not employees of the ASI, should be allowed to continue working if their physical and mental faculties permit them to do so. “Under these circumstances, the ASI would not be entitled to curtail their livelihood in this manner, particularly when the Petitioners have no other professional skill or vocation apart from photography, which they have been pursuing for the last 30 to 40 years,” the Court said. Therefore, it quashed Clause 9.3 of the ASI's 2017 policy, which prescribed 65 years as the upper age limit for licensed photographers at centrally protected monuments. items.title: New anaemia data raise questions over progress of Anaemia Mukt Bharat
items.summary: Months after releasing the latest National Family Health Survey (NFHS) factsheet without crucial data on anaemia, the Union government has finally published the figures under a separate study. They were released on Tuesday, November 24, in a study titled the Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA) 2023–2025. The data show that nearly 56% of women of reproductive age (15-49 years) are anaemic, despite a systematic intervention through Anaemia Mukt Bharat (AMB), a strategy launched in 2018. The Union Ministry, however, said that severe anaemia was observed only in less than 2% of people in the majority of the age groups. The report was prepared by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) under the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. While the government claimed that the prevalence of anaemia came down, experts point out that results of SAMPADA are not comparable with previous national surveys. An analysis of the Union Government’s scheme Anaemia Mukt Bharat, in the backdrop of survey results, shows nearly half of the funds remain unutilised.
